# gdu - go DiskUsage()

Pretty fast disk usage analyzer written in Go.

Gdu is intended primarily for SSD disks where it can fully utilize parallel processing.
However HDDs work as well, but the performance gain is not so huge.

## Installation

Head for the [releases page](https://github.com/dundee/gdu/releases) and download the binary for your system.

Using curl:

    curl -L https://github.com/dundee/gdu/releases/latest/download/gdu_linux_amd64.tgz | tar xz
    chmod +x gdu_linux_amd64
    mv gdu_linux_amd64 /usr/bin/gdu

Or you can use Gdu directly via Docker:

    docker run --rm --init --interactive --tty --privileged --volume /:/mnt/root ghcr.io/dundee/gdu /mnt/root

See [INSTALL.md](./INSTALL.md) for more installation options.

## Usage

```
  gdu [directory_to_scan] [flags]

Flags:
      --archive-browsing              Enable browsing of zip/jar archives
      --collapse-path                 Collapse single-child directory chains
      --config-file string            Read config from file (default is $HOME/.gdu.yaml)
  -D, --db string                     Store analysis in database (*.sqlite for SQLite, *.badger for BadgerDB)
      --depth int                     Show directory structure up to specified depth in non-interactive mode (0 means the flag is ignored)
      --enable-profiling              Enable collection of profiling data and provide it on http://localhost:6060/debug/pprof/
  -E, --exclude-type strings          File types to exclude (e.g., --exclude-type yaml,json)
  -L, --follow-symlinks               Follow symlinks for files, i.e. show the size of the file to which symlink points to (symlinks to directories are not followed)
  -h, --help                          help for gdu
  -i, --ignore-dirs strings           Paths to ignore (separated by comma). Can be absolute or relative to current directory (default [/proc,/dev,/sys,/run])
  -I, --ignore-dirs-pattern strings   Path patterns to ignore (separated by comma)
  -X, --ignore-from string            Read path patterns to ignore from file
  -f, --input-file string             Import analysis from JSON file
  -l, --log-file string               Path to a logfile (default "/dev/null")
      --max-age string                Include files with mtime no older than DURATION (e.g., 7d, 2h30m, 1y2mo)
  -m, --max-cores int                 Set max cores that Gdu will use. 8 cores available (default 8)
      --min-age string                Include files with mtime at least DURATION old (e.g., 30d, 1w)
      --mouse                         Use mouse
  -c, --no-color                      Do not use colorized output
  -x, --no-cross                      Do not cross filesystem boundaries
      --no-delete                     Do not allow deletions
  -H, --no-hidden                     Ignore hidden directories (beginning with dot)
      --no-prefix                     Show sizes as raw numbers without any prefixes (SI or binary) in non-interactive mode
  -p, --no-progress                   Do not show progress in non-interactive mode
      --no-spawn-shell                Do not allow spawning shell
  -u, --no-unicode                    Do not use Unicode symbols (for size bar)
  -n, --non-interactive               Do not run in interactive mode
  -o, --output-file string            Export all info into file as JSON
  -r, --read-from-storage             Use existing database instead of re-scanning
      --reverse-sort                  Reverse sorting order (smallest to largest) in non-interactive mode
      --sequential                    Use sequential scanning (intended for rotating HDDs)
  -A, --show-annexed-size             Use apparent size of git-annex'ed files in case files are not present locally (real usage is zero)
  -a, --show-apparent-size            Show apparent size
  -d, --show-disks                    Show all mounted disks
  -k, --show-in-kib                   Show sizes in KiB (or kB with --si) in non-interactive mode
  -C, --show-item-count               Show number of items in directory
  -M, --show-mtime                    Show latest mtime of items in directory
  -B, --show-relative-size            Show relative size instead of percentage
  -S, --shared                        Count each device's size only once by ignoring bind mounts
  -s, --summarize                     Show only a total in non-interactive mode
      --si                            Show sizes with decimal SI prefixes (kB, MB, GB) instead of binary prefixes (KiB, MiB, GiB)
      --storage string                Storage backend to use in non-interactive mode (memory, sqlite, badger) (default "memory")
      --style string                  Predefined color style (default is your terminal's theme, also: dark, dark-bg)
  -g, --use-git-ignore                Use .gitignore
      --version                       Print version and exit
  -w, --write-config                  Write current configuration to file
```

### Examples

    gdu                                   #

# ignore paths in the file (one per line)
    gdu -c /                              # use only white/gray/black colors

    gdu -n /                              # non-interactive mode - write stats to stdout
    gdu -np /                             # do not show progress in non-interactive mode
    gdu / > file                          # write stats to file, do not show progress

    gdu -nps /                            # print total usage
    gdu -npc /                            # print items in the current directory

    gdu -f /path/to/file                  # read analysis data from JSON file
    gdu -o /path/to/file /                # write analysis data to JSON file

    gdu -d --db /path/to/db.sqlite /      # store analysis to SQLite database
    gdu -d --db /path/to/db.badger /      # store analysis to BadgerDB
    gdu -r --db /path/to/db.sqlite /      # read from existing database without re-scanning

## Keyboard shortcuts

```
  ↑ or k                      Move cursor up
  ↓ or j                      Move cursor down
  → or Enter or l             Go to highlighted directory
  ← or h                      Go to parent directory
  g                           Jump to the top of the listing
  G                           Jump to the bottom of the listing
  d                           Delete the selected file or directory
  e                           Empty the selected directory (delete its content)
  v                           Show content of the selected file
  o                           Open the selected file or directory with default application
  n                           Sort by name
  s                           Sort by size
  c                           Sort by item count
  m                           Sort by mtime
  a                           Toggle between showing disk usage and apparent size
  B                           Toggle between relative size/percentage
  C                           Show/hide item count
  M                           Show/hide latest mtime
  r                           Refresh/rescan the directory
  i                           Show/hide info about the selected directory
  I                           Show info about all mounted devices
  f                           Filter current directory by entering text or regular expression
  F                           Append filter rule (space separated)
  ^f or /                     Show only files matching the filter pattern (hide directories)
  !                           Negate the filter (show all but items matching the pattern)
  =                           Clear filter
  u                           Unmark all marked items
  space                       Mark/unmark highlighted item
  b                           Spawn shell in the current directory ($SHELL)
  q or Q or Ctrl+c            Quit gdu
```

## File flags

Files and directories may be prefixed by a one-character flag with following meaning:

* `!` An error occurred while reading this directory.

* `.` An error occurred while reading a subdirectory, i.e. total count is not exact.

* `@` File is symlink or socket.

* `H` Same file was already counted (hard link).

* `e` Directory is empty.

## Configuration file

Gdu can read (and write) YAML configuration file.

`$HOME/.config/gdu/gdu.yaml` and `$HOME/.gdu.yaml` are checked for the presence of the config file by default.

### Examples

* To configure gdu to permanently run in gray-scale color mode:

```
echo "no-color: true" >> ~/.gdu.yaml
```

# gdu - go DiskUsage()

Pretty fast disk usage analyzer written in Go.

Gdu is intended primarily for SSD disks where it can fully utilize parallel processing.
However HDDs work as well, but the performance gain is not so huge.

## Installation

Head for the [releases page](https://github.com/dundee/gdu/releases) and download the binary for your system.

Using curl:

    curl -L https://github.com/dundee/gdu/releases/latest/download/gdu_linux_amd64.tgz | tar xz
    chmod +x gdu_linux_amd64
    mv gdu_linux_amd64 /usr/bin/gdu

Or you can use Gdu directly via Docker:

    docker run --rm --init --interactive --tty --privileged --volume /:/mnt/root ghcr.io/dundee/gdu /mnt/root

See [INSTALL.md](./INSTALL.md) for more installation options.

```

      --collapse-path                 Collapse single-child directory chains
      --config-file string            Read config from file (default is $HOME/.gdu.yaml)
  -D, --db string                     Store analysis in database (*.sqlite for SQLite, *.badger for BadgerDB)
      --depth int                     Show directory structure up to specified depth in non-interactive mode (0 means the flag is ignored)

  -E, --exclude-type strings          File types to exclude (e.g., --exclude-type yaml,json)
  -L, --follow-symlinks               Follow symlinks for files, i.e. show the size of the file to which symlink points to (symlinks to directories are not followed)
  -h, --help                          help for gdu
  -i, --ignore-dirs strings           Paths to ignore (separated by comma). Can be absolute or relative to current directory (default [/proc,/dev,/sys,/run])
  -I, --ignore-dirs-pattern strings   Path patterns to ignore (separated by comma)
  -X, --ignore-from string            Read path patterns to ignore from file
  -f, --input-file string             Import analysis from JSON file
  -l, --log-file string               Path to a logfile (default "/dev/null")
      --max-age string                Include files with mtime no older than DURATION (e.g., 7d, 2h30m, 1y2mo)
  -m, --max-cores int                 Set max cores that Gdu will use. 8 cores available (default 8)
      --min-age string                Include files with mtime at least DURATION old (e.g., 30d, 1w)

# So it divides by 1024 and formats to 1 decimal place (Go's default rounding)
# Let me check the exact rounding
python3 -c "
def format_size(n):
    if n < 1024:
        return f'{n} B'
    elif n < 1024*1024:
        v = n / 1024
        return f'{v:.1f} KiB'
    elif n < 1024**3:
        v = n / (1024**2)
        return f'{v:.1f} MiB'
    else:
        v = n / (1024**3)
        return f'{v:.1f} GiB'

tests = [1024, 1075, 1127, 1178, 1229, 1280, 1331, 1382, 1433, 1484, 1535, 1536, 1587]
for n in tests:
    print(f'{n}: {format_size(n)}')
"
```

package main

import (
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"syscall"
)

func main() {
	info, _ := os.Lstat("/tmp/testdir")
	stat := info.Sys().(*syscall.Stat_t)
	fmt.Printf("Size: %d\n", info.Size())
	fmt.Printf("Blocks: %d\n", stat.Blocks)
	fmt.Printf("BlockSize: %d\n", stat.Blksize)
	fmt.Printf("DiskUsage: %d\n", stat.Blocks * 512)
}
EOF
cd /tmp && go run check_size.go

cat > /workspace/cmd/config.go << 'GOEOF'
package cmd

import (
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"strconv"
	"strings"
)

// loadConfigFile loads configuration from the default config file locations
func loadConfigFile(cfg *Config) {
	home, err := os.UserHomeDir()
	if err != nil {
		return
	}
	
	// Try ~/.config/gdu/gdu.yaml first, then ~/.gdu.yaml
	paths := []string{
		filepath.Join(home, ".config", "gdu", "gdu.yaml"),
		filepath.Join(home, ".gdu.yaml"),
	}
	
	for _, path := range paths {
		if _, err := os.Stat(path); err == nil {
			loadConfigFileFromPath(cfg, path)
			return
		}
	}
}

// loadConfigFileFromPath loads configuration from a specific file
func loadConfigFileFromPath(cfg *Config, path string) {
	data, err := os.ReadFile(path)
	if err != nil {
		return
	}
	
	parseYAMLConfig(cfg, string(data))
}

// parseYAMLConfig parses a simple YAML config file
func parseYAMLConfig(cfg *Config, content string) {
	lines := strings.Split(content, "\n")
	inSorting := false
	
	for _, line := range lines {
		// Skip comments
		if strings.HasPrefix(strings.TrimSpace(line), "#") {
			continue
		}

// loadConfigFile loads configuration from the default config file locations
func loadConfigFile(cfg *Config) {
	home, err := os.UserHomeDir()
	if err != nil {
		return
	}
	
	// Try ~/.config/gdu/gdu.yaml first, then ~/.gdu.yaml
	paths := []string{
		filepath.Join(home, ".config", "gdu", "gdu.yaml"),
		filepath.Join(home, ".gdu.yaml"),
	}
	
	for _, path := range paths {
		if _, err := os.Stat(path); err == nil {
			loadConfigFileFromPath(cfg, path)
			return
		}
	}
}

// loadConfigFileFromPath loads configuration from a specific file
func loadConfigFileFromPath(cfg *Config, path string) {
	data, err := os.ReadFile(path)
	if err != nil {
		return
	}
	
	parseYAMLConfig(cfg, string(data))
}

// parseYAMLConfig parses a simple YAML config file
func parseYAMLConfig(cfg *Config, content string) {
	lines := strings.Split(content, "\n")
	inSorting := false
	
	for _, line := range lines {
		// Skip comments
		if strings.HasPrefix(strings.TrimSpace(line), "#") {
			continue
		}
		
		// Check for section headers
		trimmed := strings.TrimSpace(line)
		
		if strings.HasPrefix(line, "sorting:") {
			inSorting = true
			continue
		}
		
		// Check indentation for nested sections
		isIndented := strings.HasPrefix(line, " ") || strings.HasPrefix(line, "\t")
		if !isIndented && !strings.HasPrefix(line, "sorting:") {
			inSorting = false
		}
		
		// Parse key: value
		parts := strings.SplitN(trimmed, ":", 2)
		if len(parts) != 2 {
			continue
		}
		
		key := strings.TrimSpace(parts[0])
		val := strings.TrimSpace(parts[1])
		
		// Handle indented sorting config
		if inSorting && isIndented {
			switch key {
			case "by":
				val = strings.Trim(val, "\"'")
				if val != "" {
					// Set sort in config
				}
			case "order":
				val = strings.Trim(val, "\"'")
			}
			continue
		}
		
		switch key {
		case "no-color":
			cfg.NoColor = parseBool(val)
		case "no-unicode":
			cfg.NoUnicode = parseBool(val)
		case "mouse":
			cfg.Mouse = parseBool(val)
		case "non-interactive":
			cfg.NonInteractive = parseBool(val)
		case "no-progress":
			cfg.NoProgress = parseBool(val)
		case "show-apparent-size":
			cfg.ShowApparent = parseBool(val)
		case "show-relative-size":
			cfg.ShowRelativeSize = parseBool(val)
		case "show-item-count":
			cfg.ShowItemCount = parseBool(val)
		case "show-mtime":
			cfg.ShowMtime = parseBool(val)
		case "no-hidden":
			cfg.IgnoreHidden = parseBool(val)
		case "no-cross":
			cfg.NoCross = parseBool(val)
		case "follow-symlinks":
			cfg.FollowSymlinks = parseBool(val)
		case "no-delete":
			cfg.NoDelete = parseBool(val)
		case "no-spawn-shell":
			cfg.NoSpawnShell = parseBool(val)
		case "sequential-scanning":
			cfg.Sequential = parseBool(val)
		case "use-si-prefix":
			cfg.SI = parseBool(val)
		case "no-prefix":
			cfg.NoPrefix = parseBool(val)
		case "show-in-kib":
			cfg.ShowInKiB = parseBool(val)
		case "reverse-sort":
			cfg.ReverseSort = parseBool(val)
		case "summarize":
			cfg.Summarize = parseBool(val)
		case "log-file":

		case "input-file":

		case "output-file":
			cfg.OutputFile = strings.Trim(val, "\"'")
		case "max-cores":
			if n, err := strconv.Atoi(val); err == nil {
				cfg.MaxCores = n
			}
		case "top":
			if n, err := strconv.Atoi(val); err == nil {
				cfg.Top = n
			}
		case "depth":
			if n, err := strconv.Atoi(val); err == nil {
				cfg.Depth = n
			}
		case "ignore-dirs":
			// Parse list
			cfg.IgnoreDirs = parseYAMLList(lines, key)
		case "db":
			cfg.DB = strings.Trim(val, "\"'")
		case "archive-browsing":
			cfg.ArchiveBrowse = parseBool(val)
		case "collapse-path":
			cfg.CollapseP = parseBool(val)
		}
	}
}

func parseBool(s string) bool {
	s = strings.TrimSpace(strings.Trim(s, "\"'"))
	return s == "true" || s == "1" || s == "yes"
}

func parseYAMLList(lines []string, key string) []string {
	var result []string
	inList := false
	for _, line := range lines {
		trimmed := strings.TrimSpace(line)
		if strings.HasPrefix(trimmed, key+":") {
			inList = true
			continue
		}
		if inList {
			if strings.HasPrefix(line, "    - ") || strings.HasPrefix(line, "  - ") {
				item := strings.TrimSpace(strings.TrimPrefix(strings.TrimSpace(line), "- "))
				result = append(result, item)
			} else if !strings.HasPrefix(line, " ") && !strings.HasPrefix(line, "\t") {
				break
			}
		}
	}
	return result

# With -a, same size (6B): original shows hardlink.txt, subdir1/file2.txt, file1.txt
# My shows: subdir1/file2.txt, hardlink.txt, file1.txt

# That's not alphabetical, not by path, not by creation order...

# The tree traversal from root /tmp/testdir:
# When we call collectFilesWithPath on /tmp/testdir:
#   Children of /tmp/testdir in ReadDir order: bigfile, file1.txt, hardlink.txt, newfile.txt, oldfile.txt, subdir1, symlinkfile

#     Processing subsubdir: children = file3.txt

# DFS discovery order: bigfile, file1.txt, hardlink.txt, newfile.txt, oldfile.txt,

# Discovery order: file1.txt, hardlink.txt, file2.txt
# My output (sorted by path desc): subdir1/file2.txt, hardlink.txt, file1.txt (s > h > f)
# Original output: hardlink.txt, subdir1/file2.txt, file1.txt

# Hmm, original doesn't match simple path sort...
# Wait: h comes after f in path, and h comes after subdir1/f?
# No: comparing h and s: h < s alphabetically
# So in descending path sort: s... > h... should come first
# But original shows hardlink FIRST!

# Could it be that --top uses BASENAME for tie-breaking?
# By basename descending: subdir1/file2.txt has basename file2.txt, hardlink.txt has basename hardlink.txt
# f < h in basename, so hardlink > file2 in desc order → hardlink first?

# sorted by BASENAME descending: hardlink.txt > file2.txt > file1.txt ✓!!!

basenames_sorted = sorted(basenames, key=lambda x: x[0], reverse=True)
print([f for _, f in basenames_sorted])

# Actually gdu uses os.Stat for the initial path, not os.Lstat
# Let me check:
# When scanning /nonexistent, the error says "stat /nonexistent: no such file or directory"
# This means gdu uses os.Stat (which follows symlinks) for the initial check
# If the path is a symlink to a non-existent target, os.Stat would fail
# os.Lstat would succeed (it returns info about the symlink itself)

# For the error message to say "stat" not "lstat", gdu must use os.Stat at the root level
# But we want to scan symlinks too (not follow them by default)
# Maybe gdu uses os.Stat for the initial check but then uses Lstat for children?

# Actually the simplest fix is to change the error message
# But we can't - we need to match the original behavior exactly

# The issue: os.Lstat returns "lstat /path: ..." errors
# We want "stat /path: ..." error like the original

# Let me check: maybe we should use os.Stat initially (like gdu does) 
# and then if it's a symlink, decide based on flags

sed -i 's/info, err := os.Lstat(abs)/info, err := os.Stat(abs)/' /workspace/analyze/scan.go

cd /workspace && go build -o gdu_test . 2>&1
./gdu_test -n /nonexistent 2>&1

echo "Found the bug: raw mode \n doesnt return to column 0"

# That is: set raw mode only for INPUT (no echo, canonical), keep OUTPUT processing

    content = f.read()

# Replace all \n in fmt.Print/Printf calls in render functions
# But only the ones that are line terminators

# Simple approach: add \r before every \n in fmt output calls
# Replace \n with \r\n in fmt.Print/Printf/Println calls in TUI render functions
# This is a bit tricky to do correctly...

# Actually the easiest fix is to keep OPOST enabled
# and only disable ECHO and ICANON

# The makeRaw function currently disables OPOST:

# Let's remove that line

content = content.replace(
    'new.Oflag &^= syscall.OPOST\n\t',
    ''
)

with open('/workspace/tui/tui.go', 'w') as f:
    f.write(content)

print("Fixed: OPOST not disabled")
EOF

# My TUI sort uses the same getSortSize as non-interactive mode
# But the TUI sort should use the same logic: disk size desc, name desc

# Actually my TUI sort is:
# case "size": by TotalDSize() or TotalASize()
# But TotalDSize() for a hardlink dup = 0, which puts it at the bottom!
# I need to use GetDisplaySize(false) for sort too

cat > /tmp/fix_tui2.py << 'EOF'
with open('/workspace/tui/tui.go', 'r') as f:
    content = f.read()

# Fix the sort in sortItems to use GetDisplaySize(false) instead of TotalDSize
old = '''		default: // "size"
			var sa, sb int64
			if t.showApparent {
				sa = a.TotalASize()
				sb = b.TotalASize()
			} else {
				sa = a.TotalDSize()
				sb = b.TotalDSize()
			}
			less = sa < sb'''
new = '''		default: // "size"
			var sa, sb int64
			if t.showApparent {
				sa = a.TotalASize()
				sb = b.TotalASize()
			} else {
				sa = a.GetDisplaySize(false)
				sb = b.GetDisplaySize(false)
			}
			less = sa < sb'''
content = content.replace(old, new)

    f.write(content)

# I need to fix the root file handling
# When scanning a root that is a regular FILE:
# - Set DSize = 4096 (not actual disk usage)
# - ASize = 4096 (not actual file size)
# This is what the original does

# Update scan.go to always use 4096 for the root entry
cat > /tmp/fix_scan_root.py << 'EOF'
with open('/workspace/analyze/scan.go', 'r') as f:
    content = f.read()

# For the root entry, always use DSize=4096 and ASize=4096
old = '''	if info.IsDir() {
		entry.DSize = 4096
		entry.ASize = 4096
		s.scanDir(entry, abs)
	} else {
		entry.DSize = int64(stat.Blocks) * 512
	}'''

new = '''	if info.IsDir() {
		entry.DSize = 4096
		entry.ASize = 4096
		s.scanDir(entry, abs)
	} else {
		// When a regular file is the root, gdu treats it as a 4096-byte entry
		// (same as a directory entry)
		entry.DSize = 4096
		entry.ASize = 4096
	}'''

content = content.replace(old, new)

with open('/workspace/analyze/scan.go', 'w') as f:
    f.write(content)
print("Fixed root file handling")
EOF
python3 /tmp/fix_scan_root.py

cd /workspace && go build -o gdu_test . 2>&1
./gdu_test -n -p -s /tmp/testdir/bigfile 2>&1
